blocks.text: Estimate: DAU × actions ÷ 86,400 = avg QPS; × 3 = peak. Storage = items/day × size × retention. Compare each number with one machine: if it fits with headroom, don't scale it yet.

items: 1M/day ≈ 12/s · 1B/day ≈ 12k/s · peak ≈ 3× avg
Postgres primary ≈ 10–50k TPS, multi-TB
Redis node ≈ 100k+ ops/s, sub-ms
Kafka ≈ 5–10k msg/s per partition
Cassandra node ≈ 10k+ writes/s
RAM 100ns · SSD 100µs · same-DC RTT 0.5ms
WebSocket server ≈ 100k–1M connections
Too many reads → CDN, cache-aside, replicas
Too many writes → queue, batch, shard, pre-aggregate
Live updates → SSE / WebSocket + pub/sub
Many users, one item → conditional UPDATE, lock + TTL

items: How do you stop a cache stampede?
Single-flight lock per key (only one request recomputes), jittered TTLs, serve stale while revalidating, pre-warm hot keys.
Two users book the last seat. What exactly goes wrong and how do you fix it?
Check-then-act race (write skew).
Why not 2PC across microservices?
It blocks on coordinator failure and couples availability.
What is the outbox pattern?
Write the business row and an event row in one local transaction; a relay/CDC publishes the event.
At-least-once vs exactly-once?
Delivery is at-least-once in practice; make processing idempotent (dedupe by ID, upserts) to get an effectively-once result.
Kafka vs SQS?
Kafka: ordered partitions, replay, multiple consumer groups, stream processing.
How do you make an API retry-safe?
Client-generated Idempotency-Key stored with a unique constraint; return the stored result on duplicates.
Redis lock is enough for correctness?
No. GC pauses or clock issues can leave two holders.
